title: Quick check: Understanding package.json

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Understanding package.json”?
options: The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Project metadata should be justified by requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, and explicit trade-offs.
questions.answer_key: Project metadata should be justified by requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, and explicit trade-offs.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Understanding package.json: Project metadata should be justified by requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, and explicit trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Project metadata?
options: Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Document what is in scope, what is out of scope, and how reviewers can reproduce the result.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
questions.answer_key: Document what is in scope, what is out of scope, and how reviewers can reproduce the result.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Understanding package.json: Document what is in scope, what is out of scope, and how reviewers can reproduce the result.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Understanding package.json” complete?
options: Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Understanding package.json: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
